nodes.label: Module 10 — HOPE Engine
nodes.rationale: Exists so a 4-percentage-point APU shortfall (roughly $80–120k of annual margin at median census) is structurally impossible; competitors implemented HOPE as a form because CMS mandated it, but not the regulatory engine around the form.

nodes.label: Five RFA Timepoints (Admission, HUV1, HUV2, SFV, Discharge)
nodes.rationale: Auto-scheduled from M6's admission.activated so a missed window is a workflow failure, not a data-entry one; most legacy vendors implement HOPE as 'open the form when the nurse remembers'.

nodes.label: Server-Authoritative J2051 SFV Trigger (2 calendar days from visit date, D3/D4)
nodes.rationale: The clock anchors to the HOPE assessment's visit date, never to signed_at — anchoring to signature would let a clinician extend a federal deadline simply by delaying signing, silently under-reporting HQRP non-compliance. Evaluation is server-side so a client cannot suppress the SFV by under-reporting severity, and exactly one SFV is created per triggering timepoint regardless of how many symptoms cross the threshold.

nodes.label: Soft-Window + Hard-Cutoff Timepoint Enforcement (D2, D12)
nodes.rationale: Hard-blocking at window close drives chart back-dating, the worst possible response; a typed late_reason_code from a closed CMS-aligned codelist captures the deviation honestly and feeds the HQRP counter, with a rare auditable admin override past the late deadline.

nodes.label: packages/iqies-client Adapter Boundary (D5, D6)
nodes.rationale: The CMS HOPE submission spec evolves on a different cadence than the manual, so isolating transport, XML envelope and credentials in an adapter lets schema-version bumps land without touching the module. Batch-per-ProviderEntity matches CMS's batching expectation and the one-credential-per-PE-per-MAC submitter model; per-assessment HTTP would race rate limits and break per-batch acceptance semantics.

nodes.label: HopeTimepointProvider / HopeSubmissionProvider / HopeJ2051Provider Seams (D10)
nodes.rationale: Three semantic surfaces rather than one omnibus seam — a consumer wanting the J2051 trajectory should not also get the iQIES submission surface. Direct table reads would make an annual CMS manual revision a six-module change.

nodes.label: Append-Only Correction RFA with iQIES Linkage (D7)
nodes.rationale: CMS requires the original to remain on file at iQIES with the correction explicitly linked; update-in-place would destroy the audit trail and iQIES has no concept of an updated record. The Correction RFA is queued rather than sent immediately so it does not break the batch model or race the original's in-flight acceptance.

nodes.label: PPS / ESAS-r Snapshot Frozen at HOPE Sign (D8)
nodes.rationale: A live read of M9 values on every HOPE row read would let a later M9 correction silently mutate the submitted HOPE row — an audit catastrophe. The snapshot preserves what the clinician saw at sign time, which is what was submitted to iQIES.

nodes.label: Tier-Decoupled Capture (Tier 2) vs iQIES Submission (Tier 3)
nodes.rationale: Missing a timepoint cannot be recovered after the window closes, so visit-time entry must keep working during a degradation event; batch submission can wait 24 hours because the deadline is 30 days from completion. hope_assessment writes never depend on iQIES adapter health.

nodes.label: Single data jsonb for CMS HOPE Sections (D1, D11)
nodes.rationale: CMS revises the HOPE manual annually; a column-per-section schema would make each revision a six-week schema change, and a row-per-section schema would force a nine-row join on every M30 measure query. Single jsonb with TypeBox absorbs revisions as a code change, not a schema change.
